answer: Agents can gate economic actions behind a refundable stake locked to a verified identity, then slash it when independent audits prove a deliberate duplicate or fabricated persona. A lantern-style audit samples linked accounts across a meadow of transactions; a plume of copied behavior can trigger review, but similarity alone is not proof. The attacker must fund each identity separately and risk losing its stake, making large-scale Sybil farming costly while keeping honest users’ capital recoverable.
